instruction: Modify my GNOME desktop appearance by installing and enabling the Yaru shell theme from gnome-look.org.

command: gsettings list-schemas | grep -q org.gnome.shell.extensions.user-theme && gsettings get org.gnome.shell.extensions.user-theme name || echo 'default'

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to navigate to gnome-look.org, download and install Yaru shell theme, enable user-theme extension if needed, then apply the theme. Evaluator checks if shell theme name contains 'Yaru'. Similar difficulty to original GTK theme task, but focuses on GNOME Shell theme instead.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator logic correctly verifies the instruction requirement by checking if the Yaru shell theme is enabled in GNOME settings
Postconfig command properly uses gsettings to extract the current shell theme name, with appropriate fallback handling for missing user-theme extension
Metric function 'check_list' correctly uses regex pattern matching to verify 'Yaru' appears in the gsettings output
Data flow is semantically correct: gsettings output -> cache file -> regex pattern check
Expected value 'Yaru' correctly matches the instruction requirement to install and enable the Yaru shell theme
Edge cases handled appropriately: if user-theme extension is not installed or theme is not enabled, verification will correctly fail
Evaluator provides adequate coverage: enabling a theme in gsettings implicitly confirms it was successfully installed
